Create a run trace

Source: R/core-ledger-core.R
gr_trace.Rd

Create a run trace

Usage

gr_trace(
  run_id = NULL,
  meta = list(),
  system = NULL,
  owner = NULL,
  run_by = NULL,
  purpose = NULL,
  approved_by = NULL,
  governor = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'gr_trace'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

run_id

Optional identifier; generated when omitted.

meta

Named list of run-level metadata.

system, owner, run_by, purpose, approved_by

Who the run is for and who ran it: the system it belongs to, the person or team accountable for that system, the person who ran it, what it was for, and who approved it. Each is one string. One left NULL is taken from gr_options("actor"), and is NA when that does not name it either.

governor

An hr_governor() holding the limits every request recorded into this trace is checked against before it is sent, or NULL (the default) to read them from gr_options() at each check.

x

A gr_trace.

row.names

Optional row names for the result.

optional, ...

Ignored; part of the as.data.frame() generic.

Value

A gr_trace. It is an environment, so it accumulates by reference: pass the same trace to several calls and they all record into it. Fields: run_id, started, meta, actor, config, steps, calls, cached, tokens_in, tokens_out, embed_tokens, errors, budget_stop, stop_reason, spent_usd, replayed_usd, refusals, governor.

actor holds the five fields above. config is a snapshot of the options in force when the trace was made (gr_options(), with the values of api_headers left out, since they can hold credentials) and the R version, so a saved trace says what it ran under. as_json() writes started in UTC, as ISO 8601 with a trailing Z. cached counts the calls answered from a gr_cache() or a gr_replay_client() rather than the network, so calls - cached is what the run paid for. calls includes requests to an embeddings endpoint, recorded as steps labelled "embed.request". Their tokens are counted in embed_tokens, not in tokens_in, so tokens_in and tokens_out stay the size of the model calls' prompts and replies.

errors has one entry per request that failed: its step, label and error. A failure the run recovered from without losing any input also carries recovered = TRUE: the document was read in full, and gr_read_many() does not count it as failed. Only some fallbacks mark the answer partial. An embeddings request replaced by gr_embed()'s lexical fallback does when the vectors ranked the chunks a reader sent (the retrieve, rerank and iterative readers). The same fallback while gr_segment() made semantic cuts, and a proposition batch kept as written, leave the answer unmarked and say so in its $warnings. A contextual header that could not be written leaves no mark on the answer at all, and this entry is the record of it.

budget_stop is TRUE once a limit stopped the run, and stop_reason says which: "calls" for max_calls, "cost" for max_cost_usd, "tokens" for max_tokens_total, and "output", "model" or "unpriced" for the other limits of hr_governor() (see gr_options()). refusals has one entry per request the governor did not send: its label, model, the limit it would have passed, its worst-case cost worst_usd, the run's calls and spent_usd at that moment, and the message. A refused request is not a call and has no step. spent_usd is what the calls so far cost. A call to a model with no registered price (sent under allow_unpriced = TRUE) adds nothing to it, so gr_trace_cost() is the full account. replayed_usd is what the calls a gr_replay_client() answered cost when they were recorded, counted when the spending limit stopped the recorded run: nothing was paid for them, but max_cost_usd is checked against spent_usd + replayed_usd, so the replay stops at the same call. A call answered from a gr_cache() adds to neither, so a re-run through a warm cache under the same limit reads further than the run that filled it. as_json() and gr_trace_save() write budget_stop, stop_reason, spent_usd and replayed_usd, so a saved run says whether it was cut short, and refusals and governor when there are any.

as.data.frame() on a trace returns one row per request; see below.

Steps

Each request is one entry in steps. Besides its label, prompt, reply and the model it asked for (model), a step records:

params

What the call asked for: the parameters a gr_mock_client() or gr_backend_client() handler is given, which is also what a gr_replay_client() looks a call up by.

params_sent

The request as it went out, every default resolved: model, api, base_url, max_output (for a reasoning model, the larger cap its request is sent with; see gr_call()), temperature (NA when none was sent), effort, schema_name, and SHA-256 hashes of the JSON schema (schema_hash) and of the extra body fields the client and the call added (extra_body_hash). For a gr_client() it is read from the request body; for a handler, from the parameters the handler was given, which carry no extra body fields. A call answered from a gr_cache() records what would have been sent, and one a replay answered records what the recorded call sent.

tokens

input and output, plus reasoning and cached_input when the provider reported them (they are parts of output and input, not additions), and provenance: "reported" when the provider gave the counts, "counted" when they were counted here with the "tiktoken" tokenizer, "estimated" when they were estimated with another one, and NA for a reply cached or recorded before provenance was kept.

served_model, response_id, fingerprint

The model the provider said answered, its response id and its system fingerprint, where it returned them, else NA. None of them is part of a cache or replay key.

attempts

How many requests were sent for this one, retries included: 0 when a cache or a recording answered it.

started_utc, ended_utc

When the request started and ended, ISO 8601 in UTC with a trailing Z.

One row per request

as.data.frame(trace) has one row for each request the run made, in the order they were made, and none for local steps such as segmentation:

step

The step's number in trace$steps, where the full record is.

document

The document the request was about, when the run recorded one: the file name, web address or "<inline text>".

recipe

The recipe the request belonged to, when recorded.

stage

What the request was for, such as "map.answer" or "reduce".

model, ok, cached

The model, whether a usable reply came back, and whether it came from a gr_cache() or a gr_replay_client().

tokens_in, tokens_out

The size of the prompt and the reply.

usd

What the request cost, 0 when it came from a cache or failed without sending any tokens. NA when the model has no registered price, as in gr_trace_cost(), whose total the column adds up to.

seconds

How long the request took, retries included. NA for a trace written by a version of readgpt that did not time requests.

error

The error, or NA.

prompt, reply

The messages sent, each as "[role] text", and the text that came back.

effort

The reasoning effort the request was sent with, NA for one sent none. Present only when some request in the trace carried one (see effort in gr_read_spec()).

tokens_reasoning, tokens_cached_in, served_model

The reasoning and cached input tokens the provider reported and the model it said answered, NA where it did not. Each is present only when some request in the trace has it.

A request's usd prices its cached input tokens at the model's cached input rate when gr_register_model() gave it one, and at the input rate otherwise.

See also

gr_trace_summary(), as_json(), gr_answer, gr_cache()

Examples

tr <- gr_trace(meta = list(purpose = "demo"))
cl <- gr_mock_client(function(m, p) "an answer")
ch <- gr_segment(gr_example(), list(method = "sentence", max_tokens = 150))
#> Using cached ingestion for this document + settings.
#> Segmenting with 'sentence' (cap 150 tokens, overlap 0).
invisible(gr_read(ch, "What was revenue?", cl, "map_reduce", trace = tr))
#> Reading with 'map_reduce' (all|N+logN|tree) over 5 chunk(s).
print(tr)
#> <gr_trace run_20261106103547.855_999cdf>  7 steps, 6 model calls, 1118 in / 36 out tokens, 0 error(s)
#>   steps: map.answer x5, preflight x1, reduce x1 
#>   cost: $0.0000 across mock-model
#>   usage: estimated locally for 100% of requests (the provider reported none)
#>   started: 2026-11-06T10:35:47.855Z 

# One row per request, with what each cost and how long it took.
reqs <- as.data.frame(tr)
reqs[, c("step", "stage", "tokens_in", "tokens_out", "usd", "seconds")]
#>   step      stage tokens_in tokens_out usd seconds
#> 1    2 map.answer       201          6   0       0
#> 2    3 map.answer       210          6   0       0
#> 3    4 map.answer       187          6   0       0
#> 4    5 map.answer       193          6   0       0
#> 5    6 map.answer       163          6   0       0
#> 6    7     reduce       164          6   0       0
